features.title: Read one stored JSON record without loading the whole unit
features.summary: Owned fork of the native JSON storage backend: the per-record unit additionally answers synchronous per-record reads (listKeysSync, getRecordSync, getGlobalSync) so the owned storage-domain fork can hydrate one record on first read instead of materializing every record at open, and the single-layout unit answers putRecords so a multi-record batch is one whole-document rewrite instead of one per record. The on-disk format, the atomic publish protocol, the legacy whole-unit bootstrap, and every single-record write path are upstream byte-for-byte; the sync reads apply the same parse and version rules the open-time loadAll applies, and a batch publishes and rolls back as one document.

configuration.constraints: Absolute directory holding one `<unit>.json` file or `<unit>/` tree per unit; restated from the stock row because a patch replaces whole configs.

failureModes: A record document that is malformed or stamped with an unaccepted version reads as absent, exactly as loadAll reports it.
A sync read after close rejects with the backend's `closed` StorageError.
A rejected batch publish leaves the previous document and the previous in-memory state intact, and the rejection is the underlying backend/fs error: nothing of that batch is durable.
Every other behaviour is the pinned upstream code; drift is checked with scripts/native-fork-diff.mjs.

verification.testName: indexes stored document keys without reading a record
reports a foreign document as absent, exactly like loadAll does
reads a record the stock backend wrote and writes one it reads back
publishes a whole batch as ONE document rewrite
keeps the previously persisted state and rolls memory back when the publish is rejected
shows a restart every record of a committed batch and none of a rejected one
writes nothing at all for an empty batch
applies duplicate keys in order, the last value winning, in one publish

verification.reason: Host-only storage infrastructure: no browser scenario reaches a JSON unit or its document directly.

telemetry.reason: In-process file reads under the opener's existing request span: a storage unit has no network, socket, or job of its own.
